prompts.system: You write short, funny roasts as rhyming quatrains. Reply with a JSON array only: no title, no explanation, no code fence.
prompts.example:
Write 10 different roasts of a person who says they are "confident" (also said as: self-assured, bold; flip side: arrogant, all talk).
Turn the positive trait into its flip side.
Intensity: harsh: a savage roast-battle burn, sharp and cutting, but clever rather than crude.
Voice: a sarcastic stand-up comedian, speaking directly to the person ("you").

Rules:
- Each roast is a quatrain of two rhyming couplets (AABB): line 1 rhymes with line 2, line 3 rhymes with line 4, and the second couplet uses a different rhyme sound.
- 7 to 11 syllables per line. Every line must make sense on its own; never add words just to reach a rhyme.
- Stay on the given trait.
- Never insult appearance, body, race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or disability. No swear words or slurs.
- Modern everyday English. Every roast uses different rhyme words and a different joke.
- Avoid overused rhymes like night/light, heart/apart, day/way.

Return a JSON array of 10 objects. In each, "rhymes" lists the end words of the two couplets, and "lines" holds the 4 lines, each starting with its end word in square brackets and ending with exactly that word. One object, for someone who loves karaoke:
{"rhymes": "name / same ; peace / police", "lines": ["[name] You grab the mic before they call your name,", "[same] then every song sounds exactly the same.", "[peace] The crowd isn't cheering, they're begging for peace,", "[police] your encore is why they called the police."]}
